You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

import os,re,json
def load():
    d=os.path.normpath(os.environ['RLM_SESSION_DIR'])
    t=open(d+'/../../sessions/'+os.path.basename(d)+'.jsonl').read().replace('\\n','\n'); G={}
    for m in re.finditer(r'(Demo pair \d+ (?:input|output)|Test input) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):\n',t):
        k,h,w=m[1],int(m[2]),int(m[3])
        rows=[r.split() for r in t[m.end():].split('\n')[:h]]
        if k not in G and all(len(r)==w and all(x.isdigit() for x in r) for r in rows):
            G[k]=[[int(x) for x in r] for r in rows]
    return G
G=load(); di1=G['Demo pair 1 input']; do1=G['Demo pair 1 output']; di2=G['Demo pair 2 input']; do2=G['Demo pair 2 output']
# Demo1: copy at rows3-5 = shape rows2,1,0 flipped... wait earlier analysis said demo1 copy = flip where shape row0 -> out row5? do row3 = [..col3], row4=[cols2-5]+[7,8], row5=[cols3-7]: that's flipped shape rows 2,1,0. And it OVERLAPPED the 6-shape. So f(di1) must keep original too and erase uncovered 6s. My last working f did exactly that but failed demo2 due to erase logic bug; let me redo cleanly with the anchor formula nr = tb4+1+(tb4-i).
def f(g):
    h=len(g); w=len(g[0])
    c4=[(i,j) for i in range(h) for j in range(w) if g[i][j]==4]
    tb4=max(i for i,_ in c4); t4=min(i for i,_ in c4)
    o=[[0]*w for _ in range(h)]
    H=tb4-t4+1
    for (i,j) in c4:
        o[tb4+1+(H-1-i)][j]=4
    for (i,j) in c4: o[i][j]=4
    # 6-shape erased only where not covered by copy
    cov={(nr,j) for nr in range(h) for j in range(w) if o[nr][j]==4}
    for (i,j) in [(i,j) for i in range(h) for j in range(w) if g[i][j]==6]:
        if (i,j) not in cov: o[i][j]=0
    return o
print(f(di1)==do1, f(di2)==do2)

def fH(g):
    h=len(g); w=len(g[0])
    c4=[(i,j) for i in range(h) for j in range(w) if g[i][j]==4]
    c6=[(i,j) for i in range(h) for j in range(w) if g[i][j]==6]
    tb4=max(i for i,_ in c4); t6=min(i for i,_ in c6)
    o=[[0]*w for _ in range(h)]
    for (i,j) in c4: o[i][j]=4
    for (i,j) in c4:
        # v-flip anchored so its BOTTOM row = marker top row (t6)
        nr=t6+(tb4-i)
        if 0<=nr<h: o[nr][j]=4
    cov={(nr,jc) for nr in range(h) for jc in range(w) if o[nr][jc]==4}
    for (i,j) in c6:
        if (i,j) not in cov: o[i][j]=0
    return o

# New hypothesis fI: mirror the shape ACROSS ITS OWN EDGE on the side toward the marker,
# stamping flush against it, keep original, erase uncovered markers.
# Check on all three demos. d3: shape rightmost col3, marker to lower-right → mirror horizontally flush right: axis between col3 and col4: new_j = 7-j? mirror about x=3.5: j->7-j: (2,2)->(2,5) ✓ (3,3)->(3,4) ✓ (4,1)->(4,6) ✓ (4,2)->(4,5) ✓ (5,1)->(5,6)✓ (5,2)->(5,5)✓ (5,3)->(5,4)✓. YES matches d3.
def fI(g):
    h=len(g); w=len(g[0])
    c4=[(i,j) for i in range(h) for j in range(w) if g[i][j]==4]
    c6=[(i,j) for i in range(h) for j in range(w) if g[i][j]==6]
    # determine placement: try both axes; pick the one whose copy doesn't overlap the original
    srows=[i for i,_ in c4]; scol=[j for _,j in c4]
    t4=min(srows); b4=max(srows); l4=min(scol); r4=max(scol)
    t6=min(i for i,_ in c6); b6=max(i for i,_ in c6); l6=min(j for _,j in c6); r6=max(j for _,j in c6)
    o=[[0]*w for _ in range(h)]
    for (i,j) in c4: o[i][j]=4
    # horizontal mirror flush right: j -> 2*(r4+1)-1-j = 2*r4+1-j... axis 3.5 => j'=7-j where 7=2*3.5; general: j' = 2*(r4+0.5)-j = 2r4+1-j
    cand=[('H',[(i,2*r4+1-j) for (i,j) in c4]),('V',[(i+b4+1+b4-i, j) for (i,j) in c4])]
    def ok(cells): 
        return all(not(t4<=i<=b4 and l4<=j<=r4) for i,j in cells) and all(i<h and j<w for i,j in cells)
    for name,cells in cand:
        if ok(cells): o_={'H':cand[0][1],'V':cand[1][1]}[name]
    # simpler: explicitly build both, compare with demos later; first verify which candidate reproduces each demo
    return dict(H=cand[0][1], V=cand[1][1])
for k in ['Demo pair 1','Demo pair 2','Demo pair 3']:
    di=G[k+' input']; do=G[k+' output']
    cands=fI(di)
    for name,cells in cands.items():
        h=len(di); w=len(di[0])
        o=[[0]*w for _ in range(h)]
        for (i,j) in [(i,j) for i in range(h) for j in range(w) if di[i][j]==4]: o[i][j]=4
        for (i,j) in cells:
            if 0<=i<h and 0<=j<w: o[i][j]=4
        cov=set(o and [(i,j) for i in range(h) for j in range(w) if o[i][j]==4])
        om=[[(i,j) for i in range(h) for j in range(w) if G[k+' input'][i][j]==6]]
        good = all(not (i,j) in set(cov) for i,j in om)
        print(k,name, o==do, 'cov-erase-marker:', good)

    options=[]
